Last night I was busy cooking for a large get together Monday. My husband was trying to help but kept getting everything wrong. This morning I realized my behavior was toxic.
I should send this to my wife.

It's good to have moments of self-reflection.

My mother tried to teach me about being outcome focused but it didn't stick very well till I started working in management.

Sometimes, I'd give them a task and instructions on how I wanted things executed and they would just look at me confused and ask me to explain why the way I wanted something done was better than they way they wanted to do it.

So two things can happen here: you get pissy because you aren't getting your way and your way might be wrong or you accept that other people are capable of formulating ideas and completing task in a way totally different yet equally effective. It takes practice to swallow your pride, release control and let other people do their thing.

Learn to let people help you, my mom always said.

Sometimes they would ruin things terribly but giving them the freedom to make mistakes and observe the difference in outcomes, while causing me much inconvenience, helped them learn. Often they discovered better ways of doing things or helped refine and combine old ideas into new better awesome ideas.

Also there are positive and negative ways to refuse help. "I don't need help, you are in the way," can usually be transformed into, "I don't need help with this but you can help me with this." You can even anticipate some unwelcomed help and leave task just for them they are unlikely to ruin.

And remember, that the person trying to help you could be off doing any other selfish thing but they choose to be there to help you.
In your defense having someone in the kitchen when youve a lot going on can be nerve wracking. Even if theyre trying to help, sometimes theyre just so underfoot theyre in the way.

I too struggle with accepting help sometimes. I recently had surgery and soon to have another procedure so I have physical restrictions right now. My husband is being so supportive and helping out with a lot of things that are normally my job (like grocery shopping, cleaning the kitchen, etc.). I have to learn to just say "thank you" instead of "oh, thanks but you should have done it this way..." or "but why didn't you also..." and so forth.

I think, for me, accepting help in the areas I normally manage makes me feel like a bit of a failure. It's hard to see him do his job as a husband and try to do parts of what I see as my job as a wife. I hope I'm not the only one who struggles with relinquishing control and accepting my limitations?
